outline.chapter_title: Procedural Posture, Jurisdiction, and Standards of Review
outline.description: This chapter establishes the foundational context of the case, including the technical background on patents for mitigating intermodulation interference, the procedural history leading to the Federal Circuit appeal, and the specific legal standards the appellate court applies when reviewing the district court's denial of judgment as a matter of law (JMOL) and motions for a new trial.

outline.chapter_title: The '134 Patent: Claim Limitation and Expert Testimony Consistency
outline.description: This chapter presents a detailed analysis of the Federal Circuit's reasoning for reversing the quota on the asserted claims of U.S. Patent No. 7,346,134. It focuses on the 'signals of interest' versus 'interference generating signals' limitation, the reliability of Dr. Jonathan Wells' testimony regarding the RF ADC, and the court's conclusion that the substantial evidence standard was not met due to self-contradictory expert statements.
subtopics: Claim Construction of '134 Patent Claim 1: Limitation 1[a]

Holding: Reversal of Denial of JMOL for the '134 Patent

outline.chapter_title: The '775 Patent: Scope Disavowal and Insufficient Multiplication Evidence
outline.description: This chapter analyzes the Federal Circuit's reversal of the infringement finding for U.S. Patent No. 9,548,775. It examines the prosecution history regarding the three-signal limitation, the interpretation of the 'separately identifiable' construction, and why the expert evidence failed to demonstrate the required seven specific digital multiplications to satisfy the claim limitation.

outline.chapter_title: Damages, Concessions, and Final Case Disposition
outline.description: This chapter addresses the appellate court's handling of the damages award. It explains the standard of review for new trials on damages, why vacating the damages award is the necessary procedural step following the reversal of the irreversible infringement holding, and the final disposition of the appeal including the allocation of costs.
